description.purpose: The graph of one knowledge space ([#945](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/945), [#951](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/951)): every node a source of the space holds (a file's functions, classes, sections; an object and its slots; address `<source>#<anchor>`, an object's root at `<source>`) and every edge between them, resolved once and kept current, so that a question across files -- who calls this, what depends on that file, how does this document reach that function -- is answered from one store and wakes no file. A source announces each head move on `source_changed`; the hive pulls the new version with a constant number of requests (`outline`, `links`, and `near` for a file space), writes, then resolves: python imports and calls, rust `use`, markdown links, and direct addresses (`fh-<12 hex>#anchor`, `ob-<12 hex>`). An edge whose target disappeared turns `broken` with the time it broke and is counted in every answer that touches it; a neighbour by meaning is an `inferred` edge, never an extracted one. An object's nodes keep the round they were learned in: a question sees them only when that round covers its own. Since 1.1.0 ([#951](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/951)) a member's objects are a source of their own (`ob-`, pulled for `outline` and `links` only), a direct address names its node without resolving a name, and an object's nodes answer only a question whose round covers the round they were learned in. A consumer can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.1.1 ([#1085](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1085)) `./index` keeps a node's one-liner whole instead of cutting it to 300 characters: an element of the outline has no length of its own, the section that hands the outline to a model owns the budget.
description.use_when: Beside a file space (and the member's object hive), one per knowledge space: draw `source_changed` (restoring the TTL -- it is a door) and the sources' answers to `pull` into it, and ask on `in_graph` with the round of the question in the context.
description.not_in_scope: No model, no embedding request, no network; no content of a source; no tree-sitter (the extractors are the source's); no event to a consumer when an edge breaks (a librarian takes that); no graph across knowledge spaces.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed). Entry on `hop.route`: source_changed, in_pulled, in_graph. Exit: pull (`hop.source` names the source), answer.

QUESTION - body `{op: 'callers', args: {addr: 'fh-0123456789ab#def:f', limit: 20}}` on `in_graph` with hop `op`, `op_id` answers `{ok, op, op_id, addr, items: [{addr}], next, broken}`; `next` non-empty means another page under `args.cursor`.

WIRING - in a member: `./file-space -> ./graph-space` on `source_changed` with `restore_ttl` (a door: an index job in a graph space), `./graph-space -> ./file-space` on `pull` with `hop.source.startsWith('fh-')` restamped to `in_read`, and `./file-space -> ./graph-space` on `answer` with `hop.op_id.startsWith('gs:')` restamped to `in_pulled`; the same three to `./objects` for `ob-`.
